description: Piero Pelù (born Pietro Pelù, 10 February 1962, Florence) is an Italian singer-songwriter, best known as the charismatic lead vocalist and co-founder of Litfiba, one of Italy's most influential rock bands. He co-founded Litfiba in 1980 in Florence, championing the concept of 'Italian rock sung in Italian.' His theatrical stage presence and politically charged lyrics (Trilogia del Potere trilogy rejecting totalitarianism) defined the band's identity. Litfiba evolved from new wave/post-punk into hard rock with Mediterranean/Latin influences, achieving massive commercial success (El Diablo, Terremoto, Infinito). After leaving Litfiba in July 1999, Pelù launched a successful solo career, releasing albums like 'Né buoni né cattivi' (2000), 'U.D.S. – L'uomo della strada' (2002), and 'In faccia' (2006). He reunited with Litfiba for tours in 2010 and 2013. In October 2022, he suffered permanent acoustic nerve damage from a collapse during a recording session.

historical_significance: Co-founded Litfiba (1980), one of Italy's most influential rock bands
Championed 'rock italiano cantato in italiano' — Italian rock sung in Italian
Defined the Florentine new wave / post-punk scene of the early 1980s alongside Diaframma and Pankow
Litfiba was one of the first Italian rock bands to achieve international recognition
Trilogia del Potere trilogy (Desaparecido, 17 Re, Litfiba 3) is a landmark in Italian rock for political themes
Transitioned successfully from underground punk/new wave to mainstream rock without losing underground credibility
Infinito (1999) sold over 1 million copies in Italy
Continued solo career while maintaining connection to underground roots
Close ties to Diaframma — their 1985 Amsterdam EP is a key document of Florentine new wave

florence_scene_context: Piero Pelù, through Litfiba, was at the epicenter of the Florentine new wave / post-punk / dark wave scene of the early-to-mid 1980s. This scene also produced Diaframma (founded by Federico Fiumani, who attended Litfiba's first concert on 6 Dec 1980 at Rockoteca Brighton in Settignano), Pankow (pioneering EBM/industrial), Neon, Moda, Underground Life, and Polyactive. The scene was centered around venues like Rockoteca Brighton (casa del popolo), Manila (Florence), and left-wing cultural events like Festa dell'Unità. Labels like Suono Records (Mestre) and I.R.A. Records (Florence, founded by Alberto Pirelli) documented this scene. The 1983 compilation 'Italia Wiva Complication 1' and 1984's 'Catalogue Issue' (featuring Litfiba, Diaframma, Moda, Underground Life) are crucial documents of this period.
current_activity: As of October 2022, Piero Pelù suffered a collapse during a recording session resulting in permanent acoustic nerve damage. This was documented in the 2025 film 'Piero Pelù. Rumore dentro' (premiered at Venice Film Festival). His status for future musical activity is uncertain.

database_fields_to_update.bio: Piero Pelù (born Pietro Pelù, 10 February 1962, Florence) is an Italian singer-songwriter, co-founder and lead vocalist of Litfiba (1980–1999, 2010 reunion). Champion of Italian-language rock. Key figure in the Florentine new wave/post-punk scene alongside Diaframma and Pankow. Launched successful solo career in 1999 with albums including 'Né buoni né cattivi' (2000) and 'In faccia' (2006). Collaborated with Ligabue, Jovanotti, Anggun, Gianna Nannini. Suffered permanent acoustic nerve damage in October 2022.

notes: Piero Pelù is primarily known as the frontman of Litfiba. He has very close ties to Diaframma (Amsterdam EP, friendship), CCCP Fedeli alla linea (shared members), and RockGalileo (collaborators). His solo career is well-documented but he remains an underground/alternative figure despite massive commercial success. The Florentine scene (1980-1985) is the key underground period — demo tapes, EPs on Suono Records and I.R.A. Records, and compilations like 'Italia Wiva Complication 1' and 'Catalogue Issue' are crucial archival targets.
